Data Appreciation · Week 3 · Title

Collecting data fairly: surveys and samples

Who you ask decides what you find. A fair sample gives everyone a chance to be chosen; a fair question does not push an answer.

Next Generation Genius · Year 1 · Foundation

Data Appreciation · Week 3 · Goals

By the end of today

  • Explain why a sample is used
  • Spot a biased sample and a leading question
  • Write three fair survey questions
Data Appreciation · Week 3 · Idea 1

Understand it

We rarely ask everybody (the population), so we ask some (a sample). The sample must be like the population, or the answer will be wrong.

  • Asking only your friends, only the front row, or only people online is a biased sample.
  • A random sample gives everyone the same chance — draw names from a bag, or pick every 5th name on the register.

Questions can be biased too. "Don't you agree the canteen is too expensive?" is a leading question: it tells people what to say. "How would you rate canteen prices? (1 very cheap – 5 very expensive)" is fair.

Data Appreciation · Week 3 · Idea 2

Understand it

Good survey questions are short, ask one thing, and give clear answer options — including "none" or "don't know".

Data Appreciation · Week 3 · Key words

Key words

Population
everyone you want to know about
Sample
the people you actually ask
Bias
a pull that makes results wrong in one direction
Leading question
a question that suggests its own answer
Data Appreciation · Week 3 · Practice

Now you do it

  1. Look at two ways of choosing people to ask
  2. Rewrite three leading questions so they are fair
  3. Draft a five-question survey for your plan

Need a hand? Check each question: does it ask ONE thing? Could someone answer it honestly either way?

Done early? Your class is 40% girls. Design a sample of 20 that keeps that balance (a stratified sample).

Data Appreciation · Week 3 · Assessment

How you will be assessed

  • A survey about the centre's opening hours asks only the members who come on Saturday mornings. What is wrong?
  • Rewrite this question so it is fair: "Don't you think homework is a waste of time?"
  • Build your five-question survey in Google Forms and collect at least eight responses.

Your work is marked against the rubric, and you may be asked to explain your choices. Show your own thinking.
